language.script_notes: Arabic script nationwide, generally paired with English on official road signage (a common Gulf-state convention).

road_furniture.bollard_color: Rare overall, concentrated on major roads and near cities; largely absent on remote desert roads.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: More common than bollards; each reflector on Omani guardrails is red only — distinct from most countries that pair red with yellow or white.
road_furniture.line_paint: Mostly yellow side/edge lines on paved roads, with some white scattered about.
road_furniture.curb_style: Minimal outside cities; well-paved major highways.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Directional signs and distance boards are blue. Chevron curve-warning signs usually show orange-and-black stripes. White-and-black striped poles are common (also seen in the UAE).

architecture.roof_style: Flat roofs are standard nationwide, suited to the arid climate.
architecture.wall_construction: Traditional sun-dried mud brick coated in lime/gypsum plaster is the classic Omani building material in lowland areas; stone construction more common in the mountainous Jebel Akhdar region. Omani forts (Nizwa, Bahla) are iconic circular-towered mud-brick/stone structures.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Sand/tan tones matching the desert nationwide; whitewashed mosque domes and minarets.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Iconic circular-towered forts (Nizwa Fort, Bahla Fort); whitewashed mosques with minarets; traditional watchtowers dotting hilltops; terraced mountain farms in Jebel Akhdar.

nature.vegetation: Largely barren desert nationwide; a striking green terraced-farm exception in the Jebel Akhdar mountains (pomegranate orchards, rose gardens); date palm plantations concentrated along the northeastern coast.
nature.terrain: The rugged Al Hajar mountain range (including Jebel Shams, Oman's highest peak) runs along the north; vast desert (including the Wahiba Sands dunes) dominates the interior; a long coastline on the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, arid desert climate nationwide with intense sun; a striking contrast between barren lowland desert and the green terraced highlands of Jebel Akhdar.

vehicles.plate_color: Yellow plates with black text — distinctive among Gulf states, most of which use white plates.
vehicles.plate_format: Digits followed by letters, generally shorter than neighboring countries' formats.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Large SUVs (especially Toyota Land Cruisers) very common given the desert/mountain terrain.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mixed; large sections of the country are uncovered or covered only by aerial/satellite imagery rather than street-level.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Concentrated on major roads and cities (Muscat, Nizwa, Salalah); substantial gaps across the desert interior.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Gulf desert terrain, similar Arabic/English bilingual signage, shared Musandam border region with rocky hills on both sides
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Oman's yellow plates are distinctive versus the UAE's mostly white plates (sometimes with a red left strip); Oman's blue directional signage and all-red guardrail reflectors differ from UAE conventions; the UAE's Google car is typically a white SUV with a visible roof.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Arabian Peninsula desert terrain and Arabic-language signage
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Oman's yellow license plates are absent in Saudi Arabia (which uses white plates); road signage styles and coverage density also differ once compared directly.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shares a border and some similar mountainous terrain in the south
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Yemen has essentially no official Street View coverage, so any coverage at all in this border region is very likely Oman; Oman's developed road infrastructure also contrasts with Yemen's.
